question: Jim has two fair 6-sided dice: one die has faces labelled from 1 to 6, and the second die has faces labelled from 3 to 8. Twice, he randomly picks one of the dice (each die equally likely) and rolls it. Given that the sum of the resulting two rolls is 9, if \( \frac{m}{n} \) is the probability he rolled the same die twice where \( m, n \) are relatively prime positive integers, then what is \( m + n \)?

spans.text: The first die is standard, numbered 1 through 6. The second die is numbered 3 through 8.

spans.label: [RETRIEVAL.RECALL]
spans.text: The formula for conditional probability is P(A|B) = P(A ∩ B)/P(B).

spans.label: [SYMBOLIZATION.DIRECT-MAPPING]

spans.text:
First, let's figure out all the possible ways that the sum can be 9. Then, among those, how many of them involve rolling the same die twice. Then divide those two numbers.
